title: Launcher action, in line: a pusher between two curved arms shaped by the beam solver, a flooded frame, the disc flat in a roofed slot, the pull ring on top, a solid trigger that is its own sear on a hinge carrying the pull, printed in one piece on its side

findings.text: the frame is flooded: 4484 mm² solid, all but the room the moving parts sweep (8 loose bits left out)
hole 1 (⌀4.1 at -83.7, 32) is in solid frame, 3 mm of wall round it
hole 2 (⌀4.1 at -83.7, -32) is in solid frame, 3 mm of wall round it
hole 3 (⌀4.1 at 49.3, 32) is in solid frame, 3 mm of wall round it
hole 4 (⌀4.1 at 49.3, -32) is in solid frame, 3 mm of wall round it
the spring flexure's end at (0.0, 5.0) is seated on pusher by a block standing 0.3 mm² out of it, rounded into it
the hinge flexure's end at (-59.2, -8.4) is seated on sear by a block standing 6.8 mm² out of it, rounded into it
every curve's ends are in their bodies (2 on a seat)
everything clears what it isn't joined to by 0.3 mm, and each flexure touches only its two bodies: it prints free
rest to drawn: clear all the way
drawn to cocked: settles on sear at 10.22 mm (spring)
cocked to pulled: clear all the way
pulled to fired: clear all the way
fired to rest: clear all the way
drawn: nothing runs into anything
cocked: nothing runs into anything (hinge pushed 0.08° by what it meets)
pulled: nothing runs into anything
fired: nothing runs into anything
cocked: sear holds pusher against the spring flexure at any friction over 0.02 (checked at 0.1), and lets go once hinge moves 2.2°
spring: 1.26 mm thick: 3 lines of 0.42 mm
spring: 10.56 mm wide is 52.80 layers of 0.2 mm: a whole number prints as drawn
spring: at its most (11.2 mm) it sees 0.93% strain, within the limit of 1.25% (14.92 mm)
spring: finite elements give a peak of 1.11% at (-18.0, -10.2) (1.20 × beam theory), within the limit of 1.25%
spring: stopped by the ground at 11.93 mm, before its limit of 12.55 mm (by its finite-element peak)
hinge: 1.455 mm thick is 3.46 lines of 0.42 mm: a whole number prints as drawn (1.26 mm)
hinge: 10.56 mm wide is 52.80 layers of 0.2 mm: a whole number prints as drawn
hinge: at its most (6°) it sees 0.43% strain, within the limit of 1.25% (10.08°)
hinge: finite elements give a peak of 0.01% at (-73.2, -13.6) (0.03 × beam theory), within the limit of 1.25%
hinge: stopped by the ground at 8.61°, before its limit of 10.08°
the most stored is 0.043 J, in drawn; at their most: spring 7.67 N at 11.2 mm, hinge 33.5 N·mm at 6°
rest to drawn: driving spring 11.19 mm takes up to 8.20 N
cocked: let go of, pusher stays on sear, 10.06 mm from rest, which takes 7.0 N (beams and contact, friction 0.3)
cocked to pulled: driving hinge 2.15 mm takes up to 2.78 N
cocked to pulled: pusher is let go 54% of the way, with hinge moved 1.07 mm under 2.78 N, and jumps 10.0 mm
back at rest, everything is where it started
cocked to pulled: pulling hinge 1.07 mm, at up to 2.78 N, lets pusher go: the catch held 7.0 N, 0.40 of it on the finger (friction 0.3)
fired from pulled (from the moment the trigger lets go): pusher reaches 1.9 m/s; disc leaves at 1.8 m/s after 6.0 ms, with 1.3 mJ: 4% of the 36.1 mJ stored, within the 80 mJ allowed
spring: bending as far as it bends through the sequence, it sees up to 0.93% strain (large-deflection beams), within the limit of 1.25%
hinge: bending as far as it bends through the sequence, it sees up to 0.64% strain (large-deflection beams), within the limit of 1.25%
bridge 1 spans no more than the 22 mm the printer bridges
bridge 1 stands on the frame on both sides
guide 1: pusher runs in it for 16.2 mm with a 1.50 mm ridge in a groove, flanks at 45°: held across the plane
guide 2: sear runs in it for 13.3 mm with a 1.50 mm ridge in a groove, flanks at 45°: held across the plane
